description:
Use for ANY question about what an ISO 20022 message is: its official name, purpose, business
area, latest version, and the size and shape of its structure. Send a message identifier such
as pacs.008, camt.053 or pain.001. Call it even when the message looks familiar: it returns the
official name, a plain-English description, the business area and domain, the Navigator's own
functional grouping, whether the message is retired, structure statistics (total elements,
maximum depth, element counts at each depth) and the number of external code sets the message uses.

Covers the standard variant (variant 1) of each message, at the latest version held. For legacy
equivalents (SWIFT MT, NACHA, CHAPS) and the schemes that use a message, use
iso20022_legacy_and_scheme_mappings. For the list of code sets a message uses, use
iso20022_code_sets (the response's next_calls names it).

message_id.description: An ISO 20022 message identifier: four letters and three digits, e.g. 'pacs.008' or 'camt.053'. Any case works, and a hyphen, underscore, space or no separator also works ('pacs-008', 'pacs008'). A full identifier with variant and version ('pacs.008.001.13') is accepted; the response gives the latest version held and notes any difference.
message_id.title: Message Id

name: iso20022_message_details

domain.description: Product domain the business area belongs to, e.g. Payments
domain.title: Domain

name.description: Business area name, e.g. Cash Management
name.title: Name

arguments.description: The arguments to send to that tool
arguments.title: Arguments

tool.description: Name of the tool that returns the related data
tool.title: Tool

Provenance.description: Where the data comes from [3.6]. Each tool supplies its own `scope`.

data_baseline.description: Quarter of the Navigator's baseline data load, e.g. 4Q2025: data reflects that load unless stated otherwise. This is when data was added to the Navigator, not an ISO 20022 publication.
data_baseline.title: Data Baseline

Provenance.title: Provenance

elements_by_depth.description: Element counts keyed by depth, counted as total_elements is (optional elements and all alternatives included). Depth 2 holds the message's top-level blocks; depths 0 and 1 are the document wrapper. Runs from depth 2 to max_depth.
elements_by_depth.title: Elements By Depth

max_depth.description: Deepest nesting level in the message definition
max_depth.title: Max Depth

total_elements.description: All elements declared in the message definition, including the document wrapper at depths 0 and 1. Optional elements and every alternative of a choice are counted.
total_elements.title: Total Elements

closest_ids.description: Not found only: up to 5 held messages in the same business area, nearest number first
closest_ids.title: Closest Ids

code_set_count.description: Number of external code sets the message uses
code_set_count.title: Code Set Count

deactivated_in.description: Navigator data load (quarter) in which this message was marked deactivated; absent if current
deactivated_in.title: Deactivated In

description.description: AI-generated plain-English description of the message.
description.title: Description

input.description: The message identifier as interpreted by the server, e.g. pacs.008
input.title: Input

latest_version.description: Full identifier of the latest version held, e.g. camt.053.001.14
latest_version.title: Latest Version

navigator_group.description: The Navigator's own functional grouping of messages. It is not part of the ISO 20022 standard.
navigator_group.title: Navigator Group

next_calls.description: Follow-up calls that return related data too large to include here, each with the tool and the arguments to send; absent when there is nothing to follow up
next_calls.title: Next Calls

notes.description: Caveats to pass on to the user
notes.title: Notes

structure.description: Size and shape of the message definition; absent when no structure is held

title: ISO 20022 message details
